stem: Which one is the quadratic equation?
solution: A quadratic equation has degree 2 in one variable. (A) \(\dfrac{5}{x} - 3 = x^2 \Rightarrow 5 - 3x = x^3\) (degree 3). (C) \(n - 1 = 2n\) is linear. (D) \(\dfrac{1}{x^2}(x + 2) = x \Rightarrow x + 2 = x^3\) (degree 3). Only (B): \(x(x + 5) = 2 \Rightarrow x^2 + 5x - 2 = 0\), which is quadratic.

stem: Which number cannot represent a probability?
solution: Probability of any event lies between \(0\) and \(1\) (inclusive). \(\dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.67\), \(15\% = 0.15\) and \(0.7\) all lie in \([0, 1]\), but \(1.5 > 1\), so \(1.5\) cannot represent a probability.

stem: To draw a graph of \(4x + 5y = 19\), find \(y\) when \(x = 1\).
solution: Put \(x = 1\): \(4(1) + 5y = 19 \Rightarrow 5y = 19 - 4 = 15 \Rightarrow y = 3\).

stem: Determine whether \(2\) is a root of the quadratic equation \(2m^2 - 5m = 0\).
solution: Substitute \(m = 2\): \(2(2)^2 - 5(2) = 8 - 10 = -2 \neq 0\). Since the left side is not \(0\), \(2\) is not a root of \(2m^2 - 5m = 0\).

stem: If one die is rolled, find the probability of the event of getting a prime number on the upper face.
solution: One die is rolled. \(S = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}\), \(n(S) = 6\). Event A: prime number on the upper face, \(A = \{2, 3, 5\}\), \(n(A) = 3\). \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an A.P.
stem: Find the sum of the first 'n' even natural numbers.
solution: The even natural numbers form an A.P. \(2, 4, 6, \ldots\) with \(a = 2,\ d = 2\). \(S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[2a + (n - 1)d] = \dfrac{n}{2}[2(2) + (n - 1)2] = \dfrac{n}{2}[4 + 2n - 2] = \dfrac{n}{2}(2n + 2) = n(n + 1)\).

stem: Solve the following quadratic equation by factorisation method: \(x^2 + x - 20 = 0\).
solution: \(x^2 + x - 20 = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 + 5x - 4x - 20 = 0 \Rightarrow x(x + 5) - 4(x + 5) = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 5)(x - 4) = 0\). So \(x = -5\) or \(x = 4\).

stem:
Find the values of \((x + y)\) and \((x - y)\) of the following simultaneous equations:
\(49x - 57y = 172\)
\(57x - 49y = 252\)
solution: Add the two equations: \(106x - 106y = 424 \Rightarrow 106(x - y) = 424 \Rightarrow x - y = 4\). Subtract the first from the second: \((57x - 49y) - (49x - 57y) = 252 - 172 \Rightarrow 8x + 8y = 80 \Rightarrow x + y = 10\). Hence \(x + y = 10\) and \(x - y = 4\).

stem: One of the roots of the equation \(kx^2 - 10x + 3 = 0\) is \(3\). Find the value of \(k\).
solution: Since \(3\) is a root, substitute \(x = 3\): \(k(3)^2 - 10(3) + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow 9k - 30 + 3 = 0 \Rightarrow 9k - 27 = 0 \Rightarrow 9k = 27 \Rightarrow k = 3\).

stem: A card is drawn at random from a pack of well shuffled 52 playing cards. Find the probability that the card drawn is (A) an ace, (B) a spade.
solution: \(n(S) = 52\). Event A (an ace): \(n(A) = 4\), so \(P(A) = \dfrac{n(A)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{4}{52} = \dfrac{1}{13}\). Event B (a spade): \(n(B) = 13\), so \(P(B) = \dfrac{n(B)}{n(S)} = \dfrac{13}{52} = \dfrac{1}{4}\).

Sum of the present ages of Manish and Savita is 31 years. Manish's age 3 years ago was 4 times the age of Savita at that time. Find their present ages.
solution: Let Manish's present age be \(m\) and Savita's be \(s\). Then \(m + s = 31\). Three years ago: \(m - 3 = 4(s - 3) \Rightarrow m - 3 = 4s - 12 \Rightarrow m = 4s - 9\). Substitute: \(4s - 9 + s = 31 \Rightarrow 5s = 40 \Rightarrow s = 8\), so \(m = 31 - 8 = 23\). Manish is 23 years and Savita is 8 years.

If 460 is divided by a natural number, then the quotient is 2 more than nine times the divisor and the remainder is 5. Find the quotient and the divisor.
solution: Let the divisor be \(x\). Then quotient \(= 9x + 2\). Using dividend = divisor \(\times\) quotient + remainder: \(460 = x(9x + 2) + 5 \Rightarrow 9x^2 + 2x + 5 = 460 \Rightarrow 9x^2 + 2x - 455 = 0\). \(b^2 - 4ac = 4 + 4(9)(455) = 4 + 16380 = 16384\), \(\sqrt{16384} = 128\). \(x = \dfrac{-2 \pm 128}{18}\). Taking the positive value, \(x = \dfrac{126}{18} = 7\). Divisor \(= 7\), quotient \(= 9(7) + 2 = 65\). Check: \(7 \times 65 + 5 = 460\).

stem: If the 9th term of an A.P. is zero, then prove that the 29th term is double the 19th term.
solution: Given \(t_9 = 0 \Rightarrow a + 8d = 0 \Rightarrow a = -8d\). Then \(t_{19} = a + 18d = -8d + 18d = 10d\) and \(t_{29} = a + 28d = -8d + 28d = 20d\). So \(t_{29} = 20d = 2(10d) = 2\,t_{19}\). Hence the 29th term is double the 19th term.

stem: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 24 cm. The length of its congruent sides is 13 cm less than twice the length of its base. Find the lengths of all sides of the triangle.
solution: Let the base be \(x\) cm. Each congruent side \(= (2x - 13)\) cm. Perimeter: \(2(2x - 13) + x = 24 \Rightarrow 4x - 26 + x = 24 \Rightarrow 5x = 50 \Rightarrow x = 10\). Congruent side \(= 2(10) - 13 = 7\) cm. The sides are \(7\) cm, \(7\) cm and \(10\) cm.

stem: A bag contains 8 red and some blue balls. One ball is drawn at random from the bag. If the ratio of the probability of getting a red ball to that of getting a blue ball is \(2 : 5\), then find the number of blue balls.
solution: Let the number of blue balls be \(b\). Total \(= 8 + b\). \(P(\text{red}) = \dfrac{8}{8 + b}\), \(P(\text{blue}) = \dfrac{b}{8 + b}\). Given \(\dfrac{P(\text{red})}{P(\text{blue})} = \dfrac{2}{5} \Rightarrow \dfrac{8}{b} = \dfrac{2}{5} \Rightarrow 2b = 40 \Rightarrow b = 20\). There are 20 blue balls.

stem: The measures of angles of a triangle are in A.P. The measure of the smallest angle is five times the common difference. Find the measures of all angles of the triangle. (Assume the measures of angles as \(a,\ a + d,\ a + 2d\).)
solution: Let the angles be \(a,\ a + d,\ a + 2d\). Angle sum: \(a + (a + d) + (a + 2d) = 180 \Rightarrow 3a + 3d = 180 \Rightarrow a + d = 60\). The smallest angle is \(a\), and \(a = 5d\). Substitute: \(5d + d = 60 \Rightarrow 6d = 60 \Rightarrow d = 10\), so \(a = 50\). The angles are \(50^\circ,\ 60^\circ,\ 70^\circ\).
